document_summaries.summary: Sixty-month retail lease for Suite 140 at Ridgmar Crossing, Fort Worth, commencing March 1, 2023. Base rent $6,250/month, estimated operating expenses $1,100/month, security deposit $12,500. Allocates repair duties between Landlord (Building Systems) and Tenant (HVAC exclusively serving the Premises), prohibits rent offset, requires written notice by certified mail or courier, and authorizes lock changes under Texas Property Code 93.002 after an Event of Default.

document_summaries.document_type: Notice of default letter dated August 11, 2025
document_summaries.summary: Landlord asserts non-payment of $7,350 August rent plus a $367.50 late charge, rejects Tenant's HVAC credit, and states that remedies including a lock change will be exercised if payment is not received within ten days.

document_summaries.document_type: Email correspondence June 10 to August 26, 2025 (printed by Tenant)
document_summaries.summary: Tenant reports HVAC failure; property manager attributes the rooftop unit to Tenant under Section 7.2; Tenant disputes and replaces the compressor through the vendor; Tenant applies $8,400 against August rent; Landlord declares default; locks are changed on or about August 26 and a $1,500 fee is demanded for a new key.

key_provisions.title: Definition of Building Systems (Section 1.10)
key_provisions.summary: Building Systems are defined as the electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire and life-safety, and HVAC systems serving the Building generally, including rooftop equipment, up to the point of connection to the Premises.

refs.quote: heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems serving the Building generally, including rooftop equipment, risers, and distribution lines up to the point of connection to the Premises

key_provisions.ambiguity_notes: The definition includes 'rooftop equipment' but limits Building Systems to those serving the Building 'generally'. A rooftop unit that serves only Suite 140 arguably falls on either side of that line.

key_provisions.title: Landlord repair obligation (Section 7.1)
key_provisions.summary: Landlord maintains roof, foundation, structural components, common areas, and the Building Systems, but is not liable for failure to repair unless Tenant gave written notice and Landlord failed to commence repairs within a reasonable time not exceeding 30 days.

refs.quote: Landlord shall maintain in good repair the roof, foundation, exterior walls, structural components of the Building, the common areas, and the Building Systems

key_provisions.title: Tenant repair obligation for HVAC exclusively serving the Premises (Section 7.2)
key_provisions.summary: Tenant must maintain, repair, and replace all HVAC equipment exclusively serving the Premises and keep a quarterly preventive maintenance contract.

refs.quote: all heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning equipment exclusively serving the Premises

key_provisions.ambiguity_notes: Sections 1.10, 7.1 and 7.2 point in different directions for a rooftop unit that exclusively serves Suite 140. Section 2.2 separately represents the unit was in good working order at commencement.

key_provisions.title: Tenant self-help and no offset (Section 7.4)
key_provisions.summary: If Landlord fails to repair within the required time, Tenant may give an additional ten days' written notice of intent to repair, then repair and invoice Landlord, payable within 30 days. The section expressly does not permit offset against Rent.

refs.quote: Nothing in this Section 7.4 permits Tenant to offset any such cost against Rent

key_provisions.title: Independent covenants; no withholding or offset (Section 4.4)
key_provisions.summary: Tenant's rent covenant is independent and Tenant may not withhold, abate, or offset Rent for any alleged Landlord default; Tenant's remedies are damages or injunctive relief.

refs.quote: Tenant shall not withhold, abate, or offset Rent on account of any alleged default by Landlord

key_provisions.title: Events of Default and ten-day cure after written notice (Section 15.1(a))
key_provisions.summary: Failure to pay Rent becomes an Event of Default only if it continues for ten days after Landlord gives Tenant written notice.

refs.quote: Tenant fails to pay any Rent when due and such failure continues for ten (10) days after Landlord gives Tenant written notice thereof

key_provisions.title: Lock-change remedy tied to Property Code 93.002 (Section 15.2(c))
key_provisions.summary: Upon an Event of Default Landlord may change door locks in accordance with Texas Property Code Section 93.002 and must post a notice with the name and address or telephone number of the person from whom a new key may be obtained.

refs.quote: change the door locks of the Premises in accordance with Section 93.002 of the Texas Property Code

key_provisions.title: Notices must be written and delivered by hand, courier, or certified mail; email is not notice (Sections 17.1 and 17.2)
key_provisions.summary: Notice is deemed given on personal delivery, one business day after overnight courier, or three business days after certified mailing. Email does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in a written reply.

refs.quote: Communications sent by electronic mail are for convenience only and shall not constitute notice under this Lease unless the receiving party expressly acknowledges receipt in a written reply

key_provisions.ambiguity_notes: Whether Tenant's August 26 email referring to 'the August 11 email attachment' is a written acknowledgment of receipt is debatable.

key_provisions.title: Late charge (Section 4.3); attorneys' fees (Section 24.2); governing law and Tarrant County venue (Section 24.1)
key_provisions.summary: Five percent late charge after five days; prevailing party recovers reasonable attorneys' fees; Texas law governs and venue lies exclusively in Tarrant County state courts.

refs.quote: Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount
Venue for any action arising under this Lease shall lie exclusively in the state courts located in Tarrant County, Texas

legal_questions.question: Is the rooftop HVAC unit serving only Suite 140 a 'Building System' under Section 1.10 (Landlord's duty) or 'HVAC equipment exclusively serving the Premises' under Section 7.2 (Tenant's duty)?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: Determines who bears the $8,400 replacement cost and whether Landlord breached Section 7.1.

legal_questions.question: Did Tenant's June 21 email satisfy the written-notice and additional ten-day notice requirements of Sections 7.1 and 7.4, given Section 17.2's rule that email is not notice?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: Tenant's reimbursement claim under Section 7.4 depends on proper notice.

legal_questions.question: Was Tenant entitled to offset the repair cost against August rent, given Sections 4.4 and 7.4?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: If offset was prohibited, Tenant was delinquent and Landlord's remedies may have been triggered.

legal_questions.question: Was Landlord's August 11 notice 'given' under Section 17.1, and did an Event of Default under Section 15.1(a) exist before the lock change?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: The lease ties the lock-change remedy to an Event of Default, which requires written notice and ten days.

legal_questions.question: Did the lock change comply with Texas Property Code Section 93.002(c)(3) and (f), including the posted-notice content and conditioning the new key on payment of only delinquent rent?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: A non-compliant lockout exposes Landlord to the remedies in Section 93.002(g) and a writ of reentry under Section 93.003.

legal_questions.question: May Landlord assess the $1,500 'lockout and administrative fee' when no such charge is stated in the lease?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: Section 93.012 prohibits charges not stated in the lease, exhibits, or amendments.

legal_questions.question: What are Tenant's obligations and risks regarding the security deposit and the missing 2024 operating-expense reconciliation?
legal_questions.why_it_matters: Affects the net amounts in dispute and Tenant's audit rights under Section 9.3.

Subsection (h) lets the lease supersede the section to the extent of conflict.

candidate_authorities.relevance: Provides the sworn complaint and writ of reentry procedure in justice court for a tenant locked out in violation of Section 93.002, with a hearing between the first and seventh day after the landlord requests one.
candidate_authorities.quote: The tenant must file with the justice court in the precinct in which the rental premises are located a sworn complaint for reentry

candidate_authorities.relevance: Prohibits a landlord from assessing a charge, other than rent or physical damage, unless the amount or method of computation is stated in the lease, an exhibit, or an amendment. Relevant to the $1,500 lockout and administrative fee.
candidate_authorities.quote: A landlord may not assess a charge, excluding a charge for rent or physical damage to the leased premises, to a tenant unless the amount of the charge or the method by which the charge is to be computed is stated in the lease

candidate_authorities.relevance: Requires refund of a commercial security deposit within 60 days after surrender and notice of forwarding address; relevant if the lease is terminated.
candidate_authorities.quote: The landlord shall refund the security deposit to the tenant not later than the 60th day after the date the tenant surrenders the premises

candidate_authorities.relevance: Makes a landlord liable to a non-defaulting tenant for damages from the landlord's failure to comply with the lease; the 'not in default' condition is contested here.
candidate_authorities.quote: If the landlord of a tenant who is not in default under a lease fails to comply in any respect with the lease agreement, the landlord is liable to the tenant for damages resulting from the failure
